clue.text: Dotty son hit the bottle

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
to hit the bottle is to drink, i.e. tippled

explanation.surface: A son has taken to drink and gone a bit mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' reads as 'crazy', but here it means covered in dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippled work is painted or drawn in small dots, so it is literally spotted all over.

clue.text: Shoot patsy in America

definitions.meaning: a shoot growing from a root or stem of a plant
American slang for a gullible person easily fooled

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks like a verb about firing a gun, but it is a plant's side growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener's word for a side shoot from a root, and slang for an easy mark.

clue.text: Professional killer wants to find the yeti

definitions.meaning: the Abominable Snowman of the Himalayas

explanation.walkthrough: A hitman is called this for his cold nerve; the yeti is a man of the snows.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold-blooded assassin, and the snowbound creature of Himalayan legend.

clue.text: Couple having trouble in leading art gallery

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair, a couple
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A couple are having problems at a top gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like two people, but is the abbreviation for pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Madrid's national museum is one of the world's great collections of European painting.

clue.text: English agents on charge in the middle east

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first pieces on top of the next

parts.note: MI, as in MI5 and MI6, the British intelligence services
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: English spies are paid for work in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: MI5 and MI6 are Britain's secret services. The definition describes the answer as a state found in that region.
explanation.definitionFit: A state ruled by an emir is typical of the Arabian Gulf, such as Dubai or Qatar.

clue.text: On the train after getting a fare

parts.note: fare as food, as in 'board and lodging', is board

explanation.surface: A passenger is on the train once they have paid for a ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' suggests a ticket price, but it is food: BOARD as in bed and board.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aboard is to be on a vehicle such as a ship, plane or railway carriage.

clue.text: Tax abuser fiddled old masters, maybe

indicators.note: fiddled, meaning cheated or tinkered with, shows the letters of tax abuser are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tax cheat fiddled his returns on valuable paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddled' suits a tax cheat, but is the anagram signal. 'maybe' shows old masters are just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: French for fine arts; classical paintings by great European artists are an example.

clue.text: Agreeable that power line be placed under a motorway

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Agreeable that power line be placed under a motorway' (8). A + M + CABLE is clear, but no clue word fairly gives the I: 'power' is P, and 'that' is no I, so a word such as 'one' seems missing.
annotationWithheld.clue: Agreeable that power line be placed under a motorway

clue.text: Tog up to get on in equestrian discipline

parts.note: to tog up is to put on clothes, to dress
to get on is to grow older, to age

explanation.surface: Getting kitted out to compete in a horse-riding event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get on' suggests mounting a horse, but means growing older.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitive horse sport in which a rider guides the animal through precise movements.

clue.text: Climber found in dire climates

indicators.note: dire, meaning dreadful, tells us the letters of climates are in a terrible jumble

explanation.surface: A plant that copes with harsh weather conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This garden plant is a vine that scrambles up trellises and walls.

clue.text: Case for making appointment about teatime

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for appointment wraps round the other piece

parts.note: an appointment is a date
teatime is traditionally four o'clock, IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone making a date at around teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' is grammatical case. Teatime as four o'clock, written IV, is a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar this is the noun case for an indirect object, as in Latin or German.

clue.text: A fair fortune, so they say

indicators.note: so they say tells us the word is heard spoken, not written

parts.note: fortune as destiny is fate

explanation.surface: A just fortune, or so people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like 'just', but it is a noun: a village fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A village or church open-air event with stalls and games is a summer fair.

clue.text: Produced a teal robe of intricate design

indicators.note: produced means made or fashioned, so the letters of a teal robe are worked into something new

explanation.surface: Someone made a teal-coloured robe with a complicated pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produced' looks like a verb in the story, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worked out in great detail, ornate and complex, is described this way.

clue.text: In-depth photos of unknown fish

parts.note: X is the classic algebraic unknown
rays are flat fish such as skates

explanation.surface: Deep-sea photographs of a mysterious fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In-depth' suggests deep-sea photography; these pictures see inside the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiographs show bones and organs beneath the skin, so they picture what lies deep inside.

clue.text: Top surgeon in hospital department

indicators.note: in places the surgeon inside the letters for the hospital department

parts.note: A and E (Accident and Emergency) is the UK hospital emergency department
CM, Chirurgiae Magister, is a Master of Surgery, as in the MDCM medical degree

explanation.surface: A leading surgeon working in a hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: A and E is Britain's Accident and Emergency department, the ER. CM for a surgeon is an obscure abbreviation for Master of Surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak or highest point of something, its summit.

clue.text: Write about ancient city when calm

indicators.note: about means around, so the verb for write is placed round the city

parts.note: to write music or verse is to compose
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Writing about an old city when one feels peaceful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calm' could be a verb or adjective; it is the noun: self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-possession and steadiness of mind under stress.

clue.text: Listen to east-enders' promotion? Hardly!

indicators.note: London East Enders, Cockneys, traditionally drop their aitches, so the opening H goes

parts.note: to listen to is to hear
a plug is a bit of free publicity or promotion

explanation.surface: Would anyone listen to an advert from Cockneys? Unlikely!
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops the H, so 'hear' becomes 'ear. The whole clue also describes the item: with one in, you hardly hear anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stopper pushed into the ear canal blocks out sound, so you can hardly hear.

clue.text: Exercised and thawed out

explanation.walkthrough: An athlete loosens the muscles before an event; a frozen thing becomes warmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are getting heated: limbering up before sport, and losing a chill.

clue.text: It's vital for a member's standing

definitions.text: It's vital for a member's standing

parts.words: It's vital for a member's standing
parts.note: reads like a remark on a club member's status, but a member is a limb, here a leg, and standing is literal

explanation.walkthrough: 'member' suggests a club or Parliament; it is a limb, the leg, which cannot bear weight without this bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia, the main bone of the lower leg, carries the body's weight when upright.

clue.text: Like Adam's son, Edward is mortified

parts.note: like, as in 'as I was saying', gives as
Ham is a son in Genesis, though of Noah, not Adam
Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Edward is embarrassed, like a son of the first man.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Ham is Noah's son, not Adam's (Adam's sons are Cain, Abel and Seth), so the setter seems to have slipped; the letters still come from Ham.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling humiliated and full of shame is to be deeply embarrassed.

clue.text: Get a move on, darn it!

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is to hurry; the other is a polite curse, as in 'blast!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A word meaning rush or sprint, and a mild expletive used in place of a stronger curse.

clue.text: Many request its liquor

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Lots of people ask for its drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'its liquor' points to the container by what it holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden barrel holds wine, beer or spirits, so it is identified by its contents.

clue.text: Cor! Nero played as he sang

indicators.note: played, as Nero played while Rome burned, tells us these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wow, the emperor Nero performed music and sang.
explanation.walkthrough: Nero famously fiddled while Rome burned, so 'played' sounds musical, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer of soft, sentimental songs, such as Bing Crosby, is someone who sang.

clue.text: Copper rod pointlessly placed over a dome

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: pointlessly means losing a compass point, here E for east

parts.note: a rod is a pole

explanation.surface: A copper rod set aimlessly on top of a dome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointlessly' looks like 'for no reason', but it removes E, a compass point. 'placed over' in a down clue puts the pieces above A.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rounded roof crowning a building or tower.

clue.text: Declare it's a foregone conclusion

indicators.note: declare means to say out loud, so the phrase is heard rather than written

parts.note: a dead cert is a sure thing, so a foregone conclusion is a cert

explanation.surface: Someone states that the outcome is already decided.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'a cert' (British for a certainty) sounds like the answer, and to declare something certain is just what the word means.
explanation.definitionFit: To state firmly and confidently, as if the matter were settled.

clue.text: Fruit from Oman gorgeous to eat

indicators.note: from tells us to take the letters out of the run Oman gorgeous

explanation.surface: Fruit from the Gulf state of Oman, delicious to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical stone fruit has sweet orange flesh.

clue.text: Labour-saving schemes welcomed by barbers?

definitions.meaning: quicker ways of doing a job
a barber would like customers who want their hair trimmed close

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: read as two words, it is a brief haircut, quick work for a barber.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicker routes and methods save effort, and a brief trim is what a barber enjoys doing.

clue.text: It's not commonly seen as pollution

definitions.meaning: the dialect contraction of it ain't, meaning it is not

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a slangy contraction of 'it ain't', heard in colloquial speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial way of saying 'it isn't', and a stain or contamination.

clue.text: Parachute taken by dunderheaded scoundrel

parts.note: dunder-headed read as headed by the head of dunder, its first letter D
a scoundrel is a rogue

explanation.surface: A parachute grabbed by a stupid villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderheaded' looks like 'stupid', but is split: the scoundrel is headed by D, the first letter of 'dunder'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small parachute used to slow a fast aircraft, or a sea anchor, is called this.

clue.text: Greek heroine whose opponent vanished

parts.note: someone anti is against something, an opponent
vanished means gone

explanation.surface: A Greek heroine whose enemy has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opponent' is a noun in the surface, but stands for 'anti'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles' tragic heroine is the daughter of Oedipus who buries her brother against Creon's law.

clue.text: Old bobby was a stripper

definitions.meaning: an early London policeman, named after Sir Robert Peel
someone or something that removes skin or peel

explanation.surface: A former policeman used to strip for a living.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is a British policeman; both bobbies and the old nickname come from Robert Peel, who founded the Metropolitan Police. 'stripper' is a vegetable peeler, not a dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Early police were nicknamed after Robert Peel, and a kitchen tool or person that removes skins shares the name.

clue.text: Offer extension for anthem to be printed

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a tract is both a chant sung at Mass and a printed pamphlet

explanation.surface: A deal is extended so that a hymn can be published.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Catholic Mass a tract is a psalm-verse anthem sung in Lent; a tract is also a printed leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: To prolong something is to stretch it out in time, giving it an extension.
